correctness.rationale: For each side of the crown graph, zero labels are feasible exactly according to whether the opposite side has zero, one, or at least two vertices labeled 2. This gives an exhaustive seven-case partition by the pair of sidewise 2-counts. Direct coefficient-by-coefficient enumeration for n=3,4,5,6 agrees with the formula; the infinite claim rests on the analytic partition, not on the finite test.

originality.rationale: The retained claim is the all-weight Roman domination polynomial of connected crown graphs and the resulting exact minimum-function multiplicity. Same-invariant, same-family-alias, broader-family, and database searches found no statement implying this formula. The complete-bipartite polynomial is not covering because deletion of the perfect matching creates index-specific exceptions when exactly one opposite-side vertex has label 2.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard bipartite family, and an exact all-weight Roman-function enumerator is a natural refinement of scalar Roman domination. The seven-regime formula exposes the structural effect of deleting a perfect matching from K_{n,n}, and it yields the exact n-fold minimum-function multiplicity as a nontrivial consequence.
